Write the numerator as

\(\displaystyle N_n=\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}(k^2-k)(n-k)\).

Expanding,

\((k^2-k)(n-k)=nk^2-nk-k^3+k^2\).

Therefore,

\(\displaystyle N_n=(n+1)\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}k^2-n\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}k-\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}k^3\).

Using

\(\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}k=\dfrac{n(n-1)}2\),

\(\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}k^2=\dfrac{n(n-1)(2n-1)}6\),

and

\(\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}k^3=\left(\dfrac{n(n-1)}2\right)^2\),

\(\Rightarrow \displaystyle N_n=(n+1)\dfrac{n(n-1)(2n-1)}6-n\dfrac{n(n-1)}2-\dfrac{n^2(n-1)^2}{4}\).

\(\Rightarrow \displaystyle N_n=\dfrac{n(n-1)}{12}\left[2(n+1)(2n-1)-6n-3n(n-1)\right]\)

\(\Rightarrow \displaystyle N_n=\dfrac{n(n-1)(n-2)(n+1)}{12}\)

The denominator is

\(\displaystyle D_n=\sum_{k=1}^{n}k^3-\sum_{k=1}^{n}k^2\).

\(\Rightarrow \displaystyle D_n=\left(\dfrac{n(n+1)}2\right)^2-\dfrac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}6\).

\(\Rightarrow \displaystyle D_n=\dfrac{n(n+1)}{12}\left[3n(n+1)-2(2n+1)\right]\).

\(\Rightarrow \displaystyle D_n=\dfrac{n(n+1)(n-1)(3n+2)}{12}\).

Hence,

\(\dfrac{N_n}{D_n}=\dfrac{n-2}{3n+2}\).

Therefore,

\(\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\dfrac{N_n}{D_n}=\lim_{n\to\infty}\dfrac{1-\dfrac2n}{3+\dfrac2n}=\dfrac13\).

If the system of equations
\(
\begin{aligned}

\end{aligned}
\)
has infinitely many solutions, then \((\lambda-\mu)\) is equal to ...........

 

[JEE Main 2024, 6 Apr (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
For infinitely many solutions, Cramer's rule requires

\(D=0,\quad D_1=0,\quad D_2=0,\quad D_3=0\).

The coefficient determinant is

\(D=\begin{vmatrix}
2&7&\lambda\\
3&2&5\\
1&\mu&32
\end{vmatrix}\).

Expanding along the first row,

\(D=2\begin{vmatrix}
2&5\\
\mu&32
\end{vmatrix}
-7\begin{vmatrix}
3&5\\
1&32
\end{vmatrix}
+\lambda\begin{vmatrix}
3&2\\
1&\mu
\end{vmatrix}\).

Hence

\(D=2(64-5\mu)-7(96-5)+\lambda(3\mu-2)\)

\(=128-10\mu-637+\lambda(3\mu-2)\)

\(=\lambda(3\mu-2)-10\mu-509\).

Since \(D=0\),

\(\lambda(3\mu-2)-10\mu-509=0\).

Now

\(D_1=\begin{vmatrix}
3&7&\lambda\\
4&2&5\\
-1&\mu&32
\end{vmatrix}\).

Expanding,

\(D_1=3(64-5\mu)-7(128+5)+\lambda(4\mu+2)\)

\(=192-15\mu-931+\lambda(4\mu+2)\)

\(=\lambda(4\mu+2)-15\mu-739\).

Since \(D_1=0\),

\(\lambda(4\mu+2)-15\mu-739=0\).

Subtracting the first equation from the second,

\(\lambda(\mu+4)-5\mu-230=0\).

Also,

\(D_2=\begin{vmatrix}
2&3&\lambda\\
3&4&5\\
1&-1&32
\end{vmatrix}\).

\(-(\mu+4)-5\mu-230=0\),

\(-6\mu-234=0\),

\(\mu=-39\).

Therefore

\(\lambda-\mu=-1-(-39)\)

\(=38\).

Let \([t]\) denote the greatest integer less than or equal to \(t\). Let \(f:[0, \infty) \rightarrow R\) be a function defined by \(f(x)=\left[\frac{x}{2}+3\right]-[\sqrt{x}]\). Let \(S\) be the set of all points in the interval \([0,8]\) at which \(f\) is not continuous. Then ∑a∈Sa is equal to \(\quad\)...................

 

[JEE Main 2024, 6 Apr (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The term \(\left[\dfrac{x}{2}+3\right]\) can jump when \(\dfrac{x}{2}+3\) is an integer,

which occurs at even integral values of \(x\).

In \([0,8]\), these values are \(0,2,4,6,8\).

The term \([\sqrt x]\) can jump when \(\sqrt x\) is an integer,

which occurs at \(x=0,1,4\) in \([0,8]\).

At \(x=0\), the function is right-continuous on its domain, so there is no discontinuity.

At \(x=4\), both greatest integer terms increase by \(1\), so their jumps cancel:

the left-hand value is \(4-1=3\),

and the value at \(4\) is \(5-2=3\).

Thus \(f\) is continuous at \(x=4\).

At \(x=1\), only \([\sqrt x]\) jumps, so \(f\) is discontinuous.

At \(x=2\) and \(x=6\), only the first term jumps, so \(f\) is discontinuous.

At the endpoint \(x=8\), the first term has a left-hand jump, so \(f\) is not continuous there.

Hence,

\(S=\{1,2,6,8\}\).

Therefore,

\(\displaystyle\sum_{a\in S}a=1+2+6+8=17\).

The length of the latus rectum and directrices of a hyperbola with eccentricity \(e\) are \(9\) and \(x= \pm \frac{4}{\sqrt{13}}\), respectively. Let the line \(y-\sqrt{3} x+\sqrt{3}=0\) touch this hyperbola at \(\left(x_0, y_0\right)\). If \(m\) is the product of the focal distances of the point \(\left(x_0, y_0\right)\), then \(4 e ^2+ m\) is equal to..............

 

[JEE Main 2024, 6 Apr (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
For the standard hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\), the directrices are \(x=\pm\dfrac{a}{e}\) and the length of the latus rectum is \(\dfrac{2b^2}{a}\).

\(\dfrac{a}{e}=\dfrac{4}{\sqrt{13}}\)

\(\dfrac{2b^2}{a}=9\)

Also, \(e^2=1+\dfrac{b^2}{a^2}\).

\(b^2=a^2(e^2-1)\)

\(\dfrac{2a^2(e^2-1)}{a}=9\)

\(2a(e^2-1)=9\)

From \(\dfrac{a}{e}=\dfrac{4}{\sqrt{13}}\), we get \(e=\dfrac{a\sqrt{13}}{4}\).

\(2a\left(\dfrac{13a^2}{16}-1\right)=9\)

\(13a^3-16a-72=0\)

\((a-2)(13a^2+26a+36)=0\)

\(\because a>0\) and \(13a^2+26a+36>0\), we get \(a=2\).

\(e=\dfrac{\sqrt{13}}{2}\)

\(b^2=a^2(e^2-1)=4\left(\dfrac{13}{4}-1\right)=9\)

The hyperbola is \(\dfrac{x^2}{4}-\dfrac{y^2}{9}=1\).

The tangent at \((x_0,y_0)\) is \(\dfrac{xx_0}{4}-\dfrac{yy_0}{9}=1\).

The given tangent is \(y-\sqrt{3}x+\sqrt{3}=0\).

\(x-\dfrac{y}{\sqrt{3}}=1\)

Comparing the two tangent equations, \(\dfrac{x_0}{4}=1\) and \(\dfrac{y_0}{9}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\).

\(x_0=4\)

\(y_0=3\sqrt{3}\)

For a point on the right branch, the focal distances are \(ex_0-a\) and \(ex_0+a\).

\(m=(ex_0-a)(ex_0+a)=e^2x_0^2-a^2\)

\(m=\dfrac{13}{4}\times16-4=48\)

\(m^2+m=48^2+48=2352\)

\(\therefore\) the required value is \(2352\)

From a lot of 12 items containing 3 defectives, a sample of 5 items is drawn at random. Let the random variable \(X\) denote the number of defective items in the sample. Let items in the sample be drawn one by one without replacement. If variance of \(X\) is \(\frac{m}{n}\), where \(\operatorname{gcd}(m, n)=1\), then \(n-m\) is equal to............

 

[JEE Main 2024, 6 Apr (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(X\) be the number of defective items in the sample.

There are \(12\) items, of which \(3\) are defective, and \(5\) items are selected without replacement.

\(\displaystyle E(X)=5\cdot\dfrac{3}{12}=\dfrac{5}{4}\)

For two ordered positions among the five selected items,

\(\displaystyle E\bigl(X(X-1)\bigr)=5\cdot4\cdot\dfrac{3}{12}\cdot\dfrac{2}{11}=\dfrac{10}{11}\)

\(\displaystyle E(X^2)=E\bigl(X(X-1)\bigr)+E(X)=\dfrac{10}{11}+\dfrac{5}{4}=\dfrac{95}{44}\)

\(\displaystyle \operatorname{Var}(X)=\dfrac{95}{44}-\left(\dfrac{5}{4}\right)^2\)

\(\displaystyle \Rightarrow \operatorname{Var}(X)=\dfrac{380-275}{176}=\dfrac{105}{176}\)

\(\displaystyle m=105,\quad n=176,\quad \gcd(m,n)=1\)

\(\displaystyle n-m=176-105=71\)

The required value is \(71\).
